title: RuPay and Net Banking For International Merchants
summary: Learn how international merchants can accept RuPay, UPI and net banking payments from India in INR and settle abroad, without an Indian entity, under PA-CB.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


The global checkout screen is a trap. You integrate a standard US or European payment gateway, switch on Visa and Mastercard acceptance, and assume your e-commerce or SaaS platform is ready for international scale.


You launch in India. Your analytics dashboard shows massive top-of-funnel traffic, strong cart additions, and a catastrophic drop-off at the payment page.


You are bleeding revenue because you are forcing a Western checkout page structure onto a group of customers that are now used to RuPay, net banking, and UPI.


Over 90% of the Indian consumer base does not transact via international credit cards. They operate within a closed-loop, highly regulated, and structurally distinct domestic network.


To convert this traffic into actual settled revenue, international businesses must integrate the foundational[Indian payment methods for international merchants](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/how-to-accept-payments-from-indian-customers-without-a-local-entity/) , including;


1. UPI
2. RuPay
3. Net Banking


Not switching to these methods will not only lead to an infrastructural problem but also a customer behavior problem.


Fixing it requires routing transactions through localised acquiring channels. You must accept these local rails domestically in Indian Rupees (INR) and settle the funds internationally in your native currency.


##


**UPI is Dominating the Indian Payments System**


You cannot achieve success with Indian customers without adding UPI as a payment method.


[NPCI’s UPI](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/upi-full-form-meaning-how-it-works/) is already processing billions of transactions every month. It has single-handedly trained Indian customers to process payments instantly and businesses to get settlement instantly.


The actual impact for a foreign CFO lies in how UPI permanently altered the checkout expectation. Consider the structural divergence:


- **The Western Assumption** : The user types a 16-digit Primary Account Number (PAN), verifies an expiration date, inputs a CVV, and waits for a[browser-based OTP redirect](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/features/native-otp) .


- **The Indian Reality** : The user clicks a payment intent link. Their native device application (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm) opens automatically. They authenticate via biometrics or a 4-digit MPIN. The transaction settles in three seconds.


If your checkout page asks an Indian consumer for a credit card number, you introduce immediate friction. They assume your platform is outdated.


While UPI is critical to serving the interests of Indian customers, you cannot rely only on this payment method.


A standard peer-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transaction often caps at ₹100,000 (roughly $1,200).


*What happens when an Indian enterprise needs to pay a $5,000 annual SaaS license?*


The UPI rails reject the payload. When you hit the ceiling of UPI’s capabilities, you must fall back on the two pillars that handle high-ticket volume and deep regional penetration.


##


**RuPay is Quickly Becoming the Go-To Option for Indian Customers**


Overall, the Indian digital payments system is booming as the[RBI reports](https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/AnnualReport/PDFs/09PAYMENT29052025564CFE8E29164796AC1B2016508B51A6.PDF) the payment-system transaction volume grew by 44% in FY24 and 34.8% in FY25.


Among these, UPI is the dominant option, but RuPay’s volume is growing. Through massive government inclusion programs, banks issued hundreds of millions of RuPay debit cards.


If your gateway cannot accept RuPay payments internationally, you are effectively telling a massive portion of the Indian consumer base that their money holds no value on your platform.


NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) is aggressively building cross-border interoperability in regions like the UAE and Singapore.


But these strategic alliances do not automatically enable a US or European merchant using a standard Western gateway to process a RuPay card. Here’s what can happen if an Indian customer wants to process payment using a RuPay card;


- The Indian issuing bank will flag the foreign acquiring request
- Check for RBI-mandated authentication protocols
- If it fails to find them
- The issuing bank will drop the authorisation


***So how RuPay cards can be accepted when Indian customers are purchasing a product from a foreign business?***


Acceptance requires processing the RuPay card through an Indian node.


This necessity is compounded by a massive technical shift in the Indian credit market: **RuPay Credit on UPI.**


The NPCI recently overhauled UPI’s debit-only limitation, and it now allows Indians with a RuPay credit card to integrate it with their UPI profiles. This fundamentally alters the authorisation game.


- **Immediate Liquidity:** It merges the high spending power of credit cards with the frictionless, app-based authentication UI of UPI.


- **Frictionless UX:** Consumers no longer type card details. They scan a merchant QR code or click a link, and the underlying funds pull straight from their approved credit line.


- **Exclusivity** : Standard Visa and Mastercard credit cards do not possess this widespread, native integration into the UPI ecosystem.


By enabling RuPay for your Indian customers, you capture the highest-intent buyers with a credit limit to process payments seamlessly using the Indian rails and an infrastructure they also trust.


**Where RuPay Works** **Where RuPay May Not Work**


RuPay works with major international platforms that accept Discover or JCB.
Firms accepting RuPay process payments through international credit/debit rails. Several European hotel websites, regional travel portals, and niche international merchants.
These are organisations that don’t route through Discover or JCB. This means the transactions can fail if they are not processed through MasterCard or VISA.


##


**Net Banking Is the High Ticket Lifeline for Indian Customers**


Foreign merchants heavily underestimate Net Banking, viewing direct bank transfers as an archaic method reserved for manual wire transfers. In India, Net Banking is the backbone of high-AOV (Average Order Value) transactions.


When operating as a foreign vendor, to[accept net banking payments](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway-india/) from India, RBI enforces highly regulated recurring mandate rules and strict per-transaction limits on such corporate cards to prevent fraud and capital flight.


**The High-Ticket Decline Matrix**


**Payment Rail** **The Technical Friction** **The Authorisation Reality**


**Cross-Border Visa/Mastercard** RBI e-mandate (recurring) limits. Fails on subscription renewals without a localised Standing Instruction (SI) setup.


**Cross-Border Visa/Mastercard** Missing Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA). Dropped by issuing bank due to lack of domestic 3DS token triggers.


**Domestic Net Banking** Fragmentation of 90+ banking APIs. Succeeds instantly. Bypasses card network limits by authenticating directly inside the bank’s portal.


Net banking is the high-ticket lifeline. It routes the transaction directly from the buyer’s corporate bank account. It boasts incredibly high authorisation rates for massive transaction values because the risk profile is validated directly by the bank holding the funds.


Integrating net banking for international merchants introduces an engineering nightmare. India does not operate on a single, unified banking API. The country possesses over 90 active commercial banks. A foreign merchant cannot build, maintain, and secure 90 distinct API integrations. You require infrastructure that abstracts the complexity of those banking APIs into a single, unified endpoint.


###


**The Mathematics Behind FX Markup for International Transactions**


When you charge an Indian buyer in USD via a foreign gateway, you force a process called Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC).


The checkout screen displays USD. The Indian buyer’s issuing bank must convert their INR funds to settle that USD charge. The issuing bank dictates the exchange rate. They apply a punitive FX markup, often ranging from 3% to 5% above the mid-market rate.


This creates two distinct financial traps:


- **Cart Abandonment** : The Indian buyer sees a final bank charge significantly higher than the checkout price due to the hidden conversion spread. They feel cheated. They churn.


- **Treasury Leakage** : If you attempt to display INR using a basic currency converter plugin while still acquiring in USD, your own acquiring bank performs the conversion upon settlement.


You absorb the 3% FX penalty on the backend. Your profit margin erodes before the funds even reach your treasury.


**The Financial Architecture of PA-CB Settlement**


**Metric** **Global Gateway (DCC/Cross-Border)** **Cashfree PA-CB (Localised)**


**Acquiring Currency** USD / EUR / GBP INR (Native)


**Buyer Experience** Pays in INR, suffers hidden issuing bank FX penalty. Pays exact displayed INR amount. Zero hidden fees.


**FX Control** Dictated arbitrarily by card networks and issuing banks. Mapped to transparent, competitive wholesale FX rates.


**Settlement Timeline** Often delayed by cross-border clearing house friction. T+5 or worse. Predictable T+2 or T+3 direct to foreign corporate accounts.


##


**How Cashfree Offers the Best Solution for International Businesses?**


You understand the regulatory friction causing your false declines. The execution requires specific legal and technical architecture.


Historically, localised acquiring required a foreign business to incorporate an Indian Private Limited company, appoint resident directors, and open local bank accounts. The RBI modernised this through the[Payment Aggregator – Cross Border (PA-CB) framework](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/cashfree-liberalising-cross-border-payments/) .


Cashfree operates as an RBI-regulated PA-CB. This license allows us to bridge the gap between Indian domestic payment rails and foreign merchant bank accounts, completely eliminating the need for a local entity.


The transaction lifecycle operates through highly regulated nodes:


- **Localised Rendering** : Cashfree renders a localised checkout page featuring UPI, RuPay, and 90+ Net Banking options. The Indian buyer pays in INR, and you receive the money in your native currency.


- **Inward Collection** : Cashfree collects those INR funds into a heavily monitored Inward Collection Account (InCA) backed by an Authorised Dealer Category-I (AD-I) bank.


- **Cross-Border Settlement** : Cashfree executes the foreign exchange (FX) conversion at competitive rates and settles the final amount directly to your foreign corporate bank account in USD, EUR, or GBP. No separate banking rails are needed from your end, and zero authentication is required. You receive the money according to the FX spread, and that too within the stipulated timeline.


- **Tax Reconciliation (FIRS)** : Cross-border tax audits require a Foreign Inward Remittance Statement (FIRS) to prove funds originated from legitimate trade. Cashfree automates FIRS generation, solving a notoriously painful manual process for your finance team.


This flow supports transactions up to the strict ₹2,500,000 (roughly $30,000) per-transaction limit mandated by the RBI for the import of goods and services.


Cashfree takes care of the technical routing and ensures your customers can access a native checkout page interface and you receive the money with minimal friction.


Cashfree solves the authentication failure. Foreign gateways inherently rely on non-3DS flows that do not map to Indian banking standards. When an Indian issuing bank receives an authorisation request from a foreign node without the proper localised token, it drops the transaction.


We work as the domestic acquiring layer and work on;


- Trigger Native Authentication
- Push AFA request directly to the user


This ensures the issuing bank receives a fully compliant and domestically routed request. The customers see an OTP request or a biometric request. Once they approve the charge, you earn revenue.


Revenue which was earlier lost to cross-border declines will now land in your bank.

##


**Cross-Border Decline | How Transactions are Declined when Routing Overseas**


When a customer in Bangalore clicks “Pay” on a US-hosted SaaS checkout, the foreign acquiring node packages the payload and fires an ISO 8583 message across the Visa or Mastercard network. That message hits the Indian issuing bank.


The Indian risk engine instantly inspects the incoming data structure. It detects a foreign Merchant Category Code (MCC), a non-INR acquiring currency, and the absence of a localised[3D Secure](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/2d-and-3d-payment-gateway-what-businesses-should-know/) (3DS) challenge parameter.


The issuing bank drops the payload immediately. They do not do this due to insufficient funds. They do it to comply with RBI capital control directives blocking unauthenticated cross-border capital flight. The buyer sees a generic “Transaction Failed” banner. The foreign gateway logs an opaque ***Error 05: Do Not Honor.***


If you use a localised PA-CB infrastructure provided by Cashfree, here’s what changes


- The data payload originates from an Indian acquiring node
- The transaction currency is native INR
- The issuing bank recognises the secure domestic routing, triggers the mandatory Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA), either through an OTP or an in-app biometric ping.


The difference is binary: immediate rejection via foreign routing versus successful, authenticated clearance via domestic routing.


##


**Conclusion**


Succeeding in the Indian market is not a marketing challenge. Nor is it about the lack of customers. Generating demand is easy as you have access to one of the largest markets in the world. Capturing the resulting capital is a payment infrastructure challenge.


If you force Indian consumers through foreign card rails, you will fail. You will face aggressive regulatory blocks, catastrophic cart abandonment, and an unmanageable reconciliation process.


The Indian financial ecosystem demands localisation. You must offer UPI for mobile-first speed, RuPay to access the sovereign debit and credit networks, and Net Banking to clear high-ticket enterprise invoices.


Stop losing verifiable revenue to false declines and cross-border friction. Integrate Cashfree’s PA-CB architecture to securely accept local Indian payment methods, trigger compliant native authentication, and settle directly to your global bank account, with zero local entity requirements.
